title: Garage Rock
tagline: Raw riffs, short songs, and a punk spark built in a garage.
summary: Garage rock thrives on blunt energy: loud guitars, stripped arrangements, and songs built to explode in under three minutes. It grew from the urge to play loud without polished studio sheen, drawing from blues, beat music, and early punk. The sound spread through local scenes and underground radio, leaving a legacy in bands that prize immediacy over virtuosity.

pillars.name: The Stooges
pillars.why: The Stooges turned sludgy riffs and confrontational attitude into a template for raw, direct rock.

pillars.name: The Kings of Convenience
pillars.why: The Kings of Convenience showed how stripped-back, slightly chaotic riffs could still feel melodic and memorable.

pillars.name: The Sonics
pillars.why: The Sonics amplified the style with brash tone and speed, making the garage aesthetic feel ferocious and fun.
